title: How Much to Save a Month for $1 Million by 50, 60, 65
description:
How much do you need to save each month to become a millionaire? Starting at 25 with an assumed 7% yearly return, reaching $1 million by 65 takes about $381 a month, by 60 about $555, and by 50 about $1,234: over three times as much to get there 15 years sooner. In the age-65 plan you put in about $183K and growth does the rest.

Assumptions (our own illustration, not a forecast): deposits at the end of each month from age 25, a steady 7% yearly return compounded monthly, no fees or taxes. With an assumed 3% yearly inflation, $1 million in 40 years buys about what $307K buys today. Real returns vary year to year, can be negative, and past results don't guarantee future returns. Not financial advice.

scenes.say: A million dollars by sixty-five? About three hundred eighty dollars a month.
Starting at twenty-five, at an assumed seven percent a year.
By sixty? About five hundred fifty-five a month.
By fifty? Over twelve hundred thirty a month.
Fifteen years sooner costs more than triple, every month.
The twist: at sixty-five you've put in just one hundred eighty-three thousand.
Growth adds the other eight hundred seventeen thousand.
One catch: prices rise too, say three percent a year.
So that million buys what three hundred seven thousand buys today.
Start early, and raise it with every pay rise.
